title: How to reduce AI feeling when generating images.
author: CollectionOk2442
selftext: I am currently working on a visual novel by using AI. However, people have pointed out that my image assets are obviously AI-generated; so, the question is: how can I make them look less like AI-generated images?

comments.author: Bishopped
comments.body: You either spend a lot of time making your own LORAs to get a distinct and consistent style or you learn to draw.

replies.author: CollectionOk2442
replies.body: hmmmm, learn to draw is not an option. Wondering how devs here handle this

replies.author: Bishopped
replies.body:
The first. You train your own model and LORA to generate consistent styles.

Also, learning to draw is absolutely an option. No one is born knowing how to draw. AI is great but at some point you may have to accept that it can't do everything for you, especially if what you want is to not appear to be using AI (which you should disclose anyway).

If your hope is that you can achieve art which no one can tell is AI and then not have to admit to using AI you've got a whole other problem on your hands.

replies.author: dick_shane_e
replies.body: Some people have physical barriers / symptoms that prevent them from drawing. I have a friend who spent months trying to learn how to draw, but developed symptoms similar to claustrophobia (which he also has suffered) and his hand can't stay still. Not saying OP is like that, but it's something a lot of people take for granted. Not every skill is for everyone.

replies.author: mantrakid
replies.body: you could hire someone who knows how to draw

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
If you use a popular model, people will know simply because their eyes are already trained on hundreds of images generated by it.

There is no workaround unless you prompt it for a very specific style and to avoid its signature traits.

replies.author: CollectionOk2442
replies.body:
hmmm, good point.   
Would a pixel art style be better?

replies.author: KS-Wolf-1978
replies.body: Better as in "more pleasing to the eye" or "harder to tell its is AI" ?

replies.author: Boomboxbeats
replies.body:
I’m developing a game that started as “modern pixel art” style with codex, chat gtp, and auto sprite with all kinds of rules in mark down files about art style snd asset generation. I recently decided to go a completely different art style because I felt my generations were too generic looking.  I saw a trailer someone posted here and although they listed some of the same inspirations as me, ( think classic SNES JRPGS) they had an almost dead on art style and color palette as me. It’s far from the only reason I decided to reskin 3000 images and 300 sprite sheets trust me but my point is make sure you have an art style YOU love because this is a painful bandaid. 😅

https://preview.redd.it/kcl40l16a7oh1.jpeg?width=1254&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=da23b07430d61ab325cfff308bb2f22e44bc312f

replies.author: Bishopped
replies.body: And this image is still very very obviously AI generated.

Right! I knew this was ChatGPT before even reading the comment. I swear some disgruntled employee at OpenAI pissed on their training data because it loves to use these dry piss yellow any chance it gets.

replies.author: Tyalou
replies.body: For me it's also the amount of details everywhere, a real artist will know that you don't need to fill everything with tiny highly detailed elements and will make sure to only draw your attention to the key items that are related to the character's story. AI has that fear of void and will fill everything with overwhelming details. Those are looking good independently but the some of it all makes it 'very AI' like nobody knew out to prioritise work when they tackled the image.

replies.author: ArolSazir
replies.body: Make your own models, train a lora on your own drawings, if you have any, or on drawings you want to emulate (preferably with permission). You can also mix different models together, training a new model. A model trained from a mix of few popular models can have an entirely original style, depending on the weights. (Almost?) All serious as artists use their own models, not off the shelf stuff, or at least heavily modify the stock ones.

comments.author: GrumpyPidgeon
comments.body:
I pulled up a lot of research on AI gaming sentiment over the years and when polled, each year people have grown a larger distaste of AI art. It’s as if in 2024 it was some parts “oh this will really improve things” up to today’s “you’re stealing an artist’s work with regurgitated crap”

Here’s my advice: use AI to generate art that you can use as a reference or as inspiration. Prompt it to create more rudimentary artwork until it looks like something you could do in Photoshop/Krita/Inkscape/etc.   Then, closely craft it based on that photo. 

The best part? Your artwork is your own, so my interpretation is that you wouldn’t have to disclose it to Steam.

comments.author: PersonOfInterest007
comments.body: My understanding is that you can get better results by giving the AI specific reference images. But if you use reference images that aren’t at least CC0, you’re going to have people upset with you for an extra reason.

replies.author: CollectionOk2442
replies.body: hmmm, good point. I use my friends pics as reference images

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I hate to admit that it sounds like an attempt at subterfuge. Don't try and trick anyone. Just accept that you'll get hate and accusations no matter the art style you choose, even if you were to draw it yourself. You should make something that you actually want to look at. There's this 'adult hotel' game on steam where the Ai art is painfully obvious, but the hundred thousand active users don't care. They love the gameplay and the character animations.

Just make something you enjoy. Look at ANY game from ten years ago, before the huge Ai generation boom. You know what you'll see? Scrutinizing comments and angry reviews from people who felt they were owed something else, just like the people of today. If YOU don't like your designs, change them. If you do, then enjoy yourself. Someone will always be there to make shit of your day and you have the option not to succumb to their attempts.

Make a good game and there will be hate regardless. On the other hand though, someone out there will absolutely love it. This is the nature of all forms of art.
